Findings

HIGHF1INPUT accepts new connections to any portPolicy −15

Rule #2 in filter/INPUT (-j ACCEPT) accepts them from any source, whatever the policy of the chain is. Every port that no rule names is open: a service that listens on one, now or later, is reachable at once.

  • causesfilter/INPUT #2-j ACCEPT

Fix

This rule accepts every packet that reaches it, so the rules after it and the policy of the chain decide nothing. Add rules for the traffic that is needed, with a tested way back, then delete it.
  1. Delete the rule that accepts everything
    iptables -D INPUT 2
HIGHF2Unreachable rules in filter/INPUTHygiene −5

Rules #3-#5 (3 rules) are never reached: rule #2 (-j ACCEPT) ends the chain for all traffic before. 2 of them are DROP or REJECT and have no effect.

  • causesfilter/INPUT #2-j ACCEPT

Fix

Delete the rules that are never reached, or move those that must apply above the rule that ends the chain.
HIGHF322/tcp is open to any sourceExposure −5

IPv4: accepted by filter/INPUT rule #1.

  • acceptsfilter/INPUT #1-p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT

Fix

If the clients are known, accept only their addresses. If SSH must stay open to any source, limit new connections for each source: the limit counts every source by itself, so one client cannot lock out the others, and it does not touch established sessions.
  1. Replace the rule with one for the known clients
    iptables -R INPUT 1 -s <trusted-cidr> -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
  2. Or drop the connections of a source that opens more than 10 a minute, in front of the rule
    iptables -I INPUT 1 -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh4 -j DROP
MEDIUMF4FORWARD accepts traffic that no rule namesPolicy −5

No rule refuses it, and the policy of filter/FORWARD is ACCEPT. This matters when IP forwarding is enabled (net.ipv4.ip_forward, net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding): the host then routes packets between its networks without a filter.

Fix

Set the policy to DROP after the forwarding paths that are needed have rules.
  1. Deny forwarding by default (IPv4)
    iptables -P FORWARD DROP
INFOF5OUTPUT default policy is ACCEPT

All outbound traffic is allowed. This is the usual setup; an OUTPUT allowlist can limit what a compromised service is able to reach.

Recommended baseline

A complete rule set to start from, made for this host. It is not what the report measures the loaded rules against. Read it before use: iptables-restore replaces the rules that are loaded. The same text comes from iptables-analyzer --baseline.

IPv4, for iptables-restore
# Recommended IPv4 baseline generated by iptables-analyzer (iptables-restore format).
# Default deny inbound and forwarded traffic; outbound traffic is allowed.
# Apply with "iptables-restore --noflush": it replaces INPUT and keeps every
# other chain, including Docker's, intact.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-F INPUT
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -s 127.0.0.0/8 ! -i lo -j DROP
-A INPUT -p icmp -m icmp --icmp-type 8 -m limit --limit 10/sec --limit-burst 20 -j ACCEPT
# Remote administration: new SSH connections are limited per source address.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh4-22 -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
COMMIT
IPv6, for ip6tables-restore
# Recommended IPv6 baseline generated by iptables-analyzer (ip6tables-restore format).
# Default deny inbound and forwarded traffic; outbound traffic is allowed.
# Apply with "ip6tables-restore --noflush": it replaces INPUT and keeps every
# other chain, including Docker's, intact.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-F INPUT
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
# Neighbor discovery is untracked by conntrack and must be allowed explicitly;
# a hop limit of 255 proves the sender is on-link.
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 134 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "router advertisement (SLAAC)" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 135 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "neighbor solicitation" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 136 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "neighbor advertisement" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -s fe80::/10 -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 130 -m comment --comment "multicast listener query" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -s fe80::/10 -d fe80::/10 -p udp -m udp --sport 547 --dport 546 -m comment --comment "DHCPv6 client" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -s ::1/128 ! -i lo -j DROP
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 128 -m limit --limit 10/sec --limit-burst 20 -j ACCEPT
# Remote administration: new SSH connections are limited per source address.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh6-22 -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
COMMIT
  • SSH is assumed on TCP port 22; change the port before applying if sshd listens elsewhere.
  • Both families are always generated: IPv6 gets addresses automatically (SLAAC), so an unused stack must be closed too.
  • Keep a second SSH session open and apply with an automatic rollback, for example:
  • printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec iptables-restore --noflush /root/baseline.v4\n' > /root/apply.v4 && chmod +x /root/apply.v4 && iptables-apply -t 60 -c /root/apply.v4
  • printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec ip6tables-restore --noflush /root/baseline.v6\n' > /root/apply.v6 && chmod +x /root/apply.v6 && ip6tables-apply -t 60 -c /root/apply.v6
  • Persist the result with your distribution's mechanism (e.g. iptables-save > /etc/iptables/rules.v4 with iptables-persistent).
